reason: §558 in Jung's own voice: 'Adam stands not only for the psyche but for its totality; he is a symbol of the self.' Direct assertion, quote accurate, claim_type correct.

§570 frames this as alchemical tradition, not Jung's own flat identity claim, and the text is disjunctive: 'in general Adam... either is the prima materia and the arcane substance itself, or he brought it with him from paradise.' The unconditional 'is' with claim_type jung-asserts overreaches what this paragraph asserts.

§565: 'The figure of Adam readily lent itself as a biblical synonym for the alchemical Mercurius' — Jung's own historical assertion about the alchemists' usage, with his two reasons (androgyny, first/second Adam) given in the same sentence.

§565 asserts the first/second-Adam typology in Jung's voice ('his dual aspect as the first and second Adam. The second Adam is Christ'), which is the prefiguration relation in the correct direction: first Adam prefigures the second Adam, Christ.

§555: 'Adam would then be a quaternarius, as he was composed of red, black, white, and green dust from the four corners of the earth'; the quaternary structure is the paragraph's explicit theme, and §557 confirms 'Adam's quaternary nature' in Jung's voice.

§557 concludes 'he is the psyche par excellence,' which Jung endorses in his own explanatory voice ('We can therefore understand why Isaac Luria attributed every psychic quality to Adam'), and §558 independently asserts 'Adam stands not only for the psyche but for its totality.'

§557 in Jung's voice: 'Psychologically the four are the four orienting functions of consciousness' and 'all mythological figures who are marked by a quaternity have ultimately to do with the structure of consciousness.'

§590: 'As the first man, Adam is the homo maximus, the Anthropos, from whom the macrocosm arose.' Jung asserts identity outright, so the weaker 'is-analogue-of' is safely contained by the text; direction correct.

Dorn's quoted claim in §587 runs the other way: the 'fiery and perfect Mercurius' is the 'true hermaphroditic Adam' — Dorn is characterizing Mercurius, so the quote misattributes the link. Adam's hermaphroditism itself is asserted in Jung's own voice ('Adam's dual nature is reflected in his hermaphroditism').
§570 explicitly attributes the quote to the 'Gloria mundi': 'The Lord endowed Adam with great wisdom, and such marvellous insight...' Source, quote, and jung-quotes-source claim_type all correct.
§589: 'Adam's inner connection with Satan is likewise suggested in Rabbinic tradition, where Adam will one day sit on Satan's throne.' Correctly typed as a reported parallel with the named tradition.
§559, Jung's interpretive conclusion from the Book of Komarios: 'Here the statue evidently denotes the end-product of the process, the lapis Philosophorum or its equivalent.'

§567, Jung's own conclusion from the Kephalaia extracts: 'It is clear from these extracts that the statue or pillar is either the perfect Primordial Man or at least his body, both at the beginning of creation and at the end of time.'

§568 correctly attributes to the Zohar: 'the Haye Sarah on Genesis 28:22 says that Malchuth is called the "statue" when she is united with Tifereth' — the statue corresponds to the Tifereth-Malchuth union, which Jung then equates with the lapis as a union of male and female.
§569 in Jung's voice: 'The statue stands for the inert materiality of Adam, who still needs an animating soul' — the soulless body; §567 likewise allows the statue to be 'at least his body.'

§589, Jung's own (hedged but asserted) inference: 'The daemonic Lilith seems to be a certain aspect of Adam, for the legend says that she was created with him from the same earth.' Direction correct: Lilith as aspect of Adam.
§602 opens in Jung's voice: 'The "old Adam" corresponds to the primitive man, the "shadow" of our present-day consciousness.' Exact match of subject, relation, and object.

§600: 'By his equation "old Adam" = Adam Kadmon the author has contaminated two opposites' — Jung himself asserts that the text contaminates the two figures, which is precisely what 'contaminated-with' encodes; Jung's point is that they are opposites, not identical.
§592: the speaker is the Shulamite as 'the feminine personification of the prima materia in the nigredo state,' and 'Psychologically this dark figure is the unconscious anima.'

§592 says 'The black Shulamite in our text corresponds to Malchuth as a widow, who awaits union with Tifereth' — she corresponds to Malchuth alone, awaiting the union; Adam Kadmon takes the place of Tifereth. Mapping her to the combined Tifereth-Malchuth pair conflates one pole with the syzygy.

§573, reporting the Chinese parallel: P'an Ku 'changed himself into the earth with all its creatures and thus proved to be a real homo maximus and Anthropos.' Correctly typed as a reported cross-cultural parallel.

§605 says 'In the idea of the homo maximus the Above and Below of creation are reunited' — the Anthropos embodies the reunion of opposites; 'unites the union-of-opposites' is a doubled formulation the text does not assert.
